d: A spicy vegetable and baked bean relish born in the townships of Johannesburg, served with pap and grilled meats.
s: Sauté the onion, garlic and chili in the oil.
Add the curry powder and peppers; cook 5 minutes.
Add the carrots and tomatoes; cook 10 minutes.
Stir in the beans and simmer 5 minutes.
Season with salt and serve hot or cold.

d: A whole pig stuffed with lemongrass, garlic, green onions and pepper, spit-roasted over charcoal until the skin is glossy and crackling — so fragrant it is eaten without sauce.
i: Rolled skin-on pork belly (or suckling pig)
s: Rub the inside with salt, pepper and soy sauce.
Stuff with lemongrass, garlic, green onions and bay leaves; roll and tie tightly.
Dry the skin in the fridge overnight.
Spit-roast or oven-roast 3 hours 30 minutes at 160 °C, basting with the soda.
Raise to 230 °C for 20 minutes to crackle the skin.
Let rest, then slice.

d: A brioche studded with kirsch-soaked raisins, baked in a fluted glazed-clay ring mold and decorated with almonds and icing sugar.
s: Knead the flour, milk, yeast, sugar, eggs and salt, then work in the butter; let rise 1 hour.
Work in the drained raisins.
Butter the mold and place an almond in the bottom of each flute.
Lay the dough in as a ring; let rise 1 hour 30 minutes.
Bake 45 minutes at 180 °C.
Unmold and dust with icing sugar.

d: A shortcrust shell filled with eggs, crème fraîche and smoked bacon — the historic specialty of Lorraine, made without cheese in the original version.
s: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Line a pan with the pastry and prick it.
Blind-bake the crust 10 minutes.
Brown the lardons in a dry pan, then drain.
Beat the eggs with the cream, milk, nutmeg, pepper and very little salt.
Scatter the lardons over the crust and pour in the custard.
Bake 30 minutes at 180 °C until golden and set.

d: Steamed dumplings with a translucent wheat-starch and tapioca wrapper, filled with shrimp and bamboo shoots — the centerpiece of Cantonese dim sum.
s: Coarsely chop half the shrimp and leave the rest in pieces.
Mix with the bamboo, sesame oil, sugar, salt and pepper; refrigerate.
Pour the boiling water over the starches, stir, add the lard and knead.
Divide into 10 g balls and flatten into thin discs with the flat of a cleaver.
Fill and pleat into a fan (10 to 12 pleats).
Steam over high heat 6 to 7 minutes until translucent.

d: Tonnarelli or spaghetti coated in a cream of pecorino romano and toasted black pepper, emulsified with the pasta water.
s: Cook the pasta in a small amount of lightly salted water.
Toast the pepper in a large dry pan, then add a ladle of pasta water.
Mix the pecorino with a little warm pasta water to make a cream.
Transfer the al dente pasta to the pan and toss with the peppery water.
Off the heat, add the pecorino cream, tossing briskly.
Adjust with pasta water until the sauce coats the pasta; serve immediately.

d: A flaky flatbread stretched paper-thin, folded and cooked on a griddle, served with dhal or curry — breakfast at Malaysia’s mamak stalls.
s: Knead the flour, water, condensed milk, egg and salt for 10 minutes.
Divide into 6 balls, coat with ghee and rest at least 4 hours.
Stretch each ball on an oiled surface until translucent.
Fold into a square to create layers.
Cook 2 minutes per side on a buttered griddle, scrunch to fluff and serve with the dhal.

d: Small fried corn tortillas that puff up, topped with shredded chicken, cabbage, tomato and habanero-pickled onions.
s: Warm the chicken with the recado and a little water.
Mix the masa, flour, salt and water; shape small 10 cm tortillas.
Fry them 1 minute at 180 °C until they puff.
Drain.
Top with cabbage, tomato, chicken and pickled onions.

d: Strings of walnuts dipped several times in grape juice thickened with flour (tatara), then dried — a harvest treat from Kakheti.
s: Thread the walnuts onto 30 cm strings, leaving a loop.
Whisk the flour into 500 ml of cold juice.
Bring the rest of the juice to a boil with the sugar and whisk in the flour mixture.
Cook 15 minutes, stirring, until thick as custard (tatara).
Dip the strings in the tatara, let drip 5 minutes, and repeat 3 times.
Hang to dry for 5 to 7 days in a dry, airy place.

d: Beef stewed in red wine and tomato with a mountain of whole pearl onions, scented with cinnamon, bay leaf and allspice.
s: Sear the beef in the oil and set aside.
Brown the whole pearl onions in the same pot.
Return the meat; add the garlic, tomato paste, wine and vinegar.
Add the tomatoes and spices, cover and simmer 2 to 2½ hours without stirring the onions.
Let the sauce reduce until it coats; serve with bread or pasta.

d: Pakistani chicken cooked quickly with tomatoes, ginger, garlic, chilies and spices in a karahi.
s: Sear the chicken in the oil until lightly colored.
Add the garlic, ginger and spices.
Add the tomatoes and cover for 15 minutes.
Uncover and cook over high heat until the sauce reduces and coats the chicken.
Add green chilies and fresh cilantro if desired.

d: Heart-shaped French cookies made of puff pastry and sugar, adapted here with ready-made pastry.
s: Mix the sugar and cinnamon. Sprinkle half on the counter and roll the cold pastry into a rectangle.
Sprinkle the rest over the pastry; roll both long sides toward the middle, then press the two rolls together.
Chill 20 minutes. Slice into 12 pieces ½ inch thick and space them on a baking sheet.
Bake at 200 °C for about 15 to 18 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and caramelized. Cool on a rack.

d: Mexican pork cooked slowly, then browned in its own fat; a home version with less lard.
s: Put the pork, lard, orange juice, quartered onion, garlic, bay leaf, water and salt in a Dutch oven.
Cover and simmer very gently 2½ to 3 hours, until the meat shreds; add a little water if it dries too early.
Remove the aromatics, uncover and let the liquid evaporate. Brown the pieces in the remaining fat, turning them.
Shred coarsely and serve with tortillas, onion, cilantro and salsa.

d: Grape leaves stuffed with meat, rice and herbs, gently simmered.
s: Mix the meat, rice, onion, herbs and tomato.
Place a small portion on each leaf and roll up tightly.
Pack the dolmas snugly in a saucepan.
Pour in the broth and weigh down with an upside-down plate.
Simmer over low heat 50 to 60 minutes.

d: Pork marinated with guajillo chilies and achiote, roasted on a vertical spit (trompo) inherited from Lebanese immigrants, served in small tacos with pineapple, onion and cilantro.
s: Rehydrate the guajillos and blend them with the achiote, vinegar, pineapple juice, garlic, spices and salt.
Marinate the pork overnight.
Stack the slices on a vertical skewer, or bake them tightly layered in a loaf pan 1 hour at 200 °C.
Slice thinly and sear on a griddle.
Grill the pineapple.
Serve on doubled tortillas with pineapple, onion, cilantro, salsa and lime.

d: A baked chickpea flour flan sprinkled with cumin and harissa and served in bread — an Oran street snack inherited from the Spanish calentita.
s: Whisk the chickpea flour with the water, oil, egg and salt.
Let rest 30 minutes.
Pour into an oiled dish to a depth of 2 cm.
Brush the top with egg or oil.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes at 220 °C until golden on top.
Cut into squares, sprinkle with cumin and serve with harissa, in a sandwich if you like.

d: A Tunisian salad of grilled peppers and tomatoes, chopped and seasoned; tuna and eggs offered as garnish.
s: Broil the peppers, tomatoes and garlic, turning, until the skins blister; allow 20 to 25 minutes.
Cover the peppers in a bowl for 10 minutes, then peel and seed. Peel the tomatoes and remove excess liquid.
Chop the vegetables with a knife without puréeing. Mash the cooked garlic.
Mix with the oil, lemon, caraway and salt. Let rest 20 minutes to blend the flavors.
Serve on its own or with tuna, olives and wedges of eggs hard-boiled for 10 minutes.

d: Sauerkraut braised in Riesling with juniper berries, served with Strasbourg sausages, smoked bacon, smoked pork shoulder and steamed potatoes.
s: Soften the onions in the fat in a large Dutch oven.
Add the sauerkraut, juniper, bay leaf, Riesling and 200 ml of water.
Bury the pork shoulder and bacon; cover and cook 2 hours over low heat.
Add the Montbéliard sausages 40 minutes before the end.
Steam the potatoes; poach the Strasbourg sausages 10 minutes in barely simmering water.
Serve the sauerkraut surrounded by the sliced meats and potatoes.

d: Wild greens cooked with onion and tomato, the traditional partner of oshifima in northern Namibia.
s: Sauté the onion in the oil.
Add the tomato and cook 3 minutes.
Add the greens and a splash of water; cover.
Cook 10 minutes over low heat; season with salt.
Serve with oshifima.

d: Tiny pasta parcels filled with pork loin, mortadella, prosciutto and Parmesan, served in capon broth — a Christmas dish in Bologna and Modena.
s: Make a capon and beef broth simmered for 3 hours; strain it.
Finely chop the pork, mortadella and prosciutto; mix with the Parmesan, 1 egg and nutmeg.
Knead the flour with 2 eggs; roll into a very thin sheet.
Cut 3 cm squares, add a hazelnut of filling and fold into triangles.
Wrap around your finger and pinch the tips together.
Cook the tortellini 3 minutes in the boiling broth and serve in the broth.

d: Round rice noodles served with an aromatic master brine (lu shui), slices of braised beef or pork, fried peanuts and pickled beans, from Guangxi.
i: Star anise, cinnamon, licorice root, fennel
s: Braise the meat 1 hour 30 minutes in water with soy sauce and spices to make the brine.
Slice the meat thinly.
Blanch the noodles 1 minute.
Put them in bowls with a ladle of brine.
Top with meat, peanuts, pickled beans, scallions and cilantro.
Add chili oil and a little bone broth if desired.

d: Semolina pastry diamonds filled with date paste, fried and soaked in a honey and orange blossom syrup — the pride of Kairouan’s pastry makers.
s: Rub the semolina with the oil, let rest 1 hour, then moisten with salted water to form a dough.
Mix the date paste with cinnamon and orange blossom water; roll into ropes.
Flatten the dough, lay a date rope in the center and close it up.
Roll into an even log and cut into diamonds.
Fry at 170 °C until golden.
Plunge immediately into warm honey scented with orange blossom.

d: A frothy English dessert of cream, sugar, lemon and white wine; a modern version served in glasses.
s: Mix the wine, sugar, lemon juice and zest until the sugar dissolves.
Chill the mixture and the cream in the fridge for 20 minutes.
Whip the cream to soft peaks without turning it into butter.
Gradually add the wine mixture, whisking briefly, then divide among four glasses.
Chill 1 hour and serve the same day. The wine keeps its alcohol since the dessert is not cooked.

d: Chicken braised in a sweet-spicy soy sauce with potatoes, carrots, dried chilies and dangmyeon noodles, born in Andong’s market.
s: Blanch the chicken 3 minutes and rinse.
Cook it with 700 ml of water, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, ginger and dried chilies for 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes and carrot; cook 15 minutes.
Add the onion and drained noodles; cook 5 minutes.
Add the green chilies and sesame oil.
Serve once the noodles have soaked up the glossy sauce.

d: Short vermicelli cooked like a paella in fish stock with shrimp, squid and monkfish until the tips curl up, served with allioli.
s: Sear the shrimp in the oiled paella pan; set aside.
Sauté the squid and monkfish, then the garlic and tomato.
Add the fideos and toast them 2 minutes.
Add the paprika, saffron and boiling stock; cook 10 minutes over high heat without stirring.
Arrange the shrimp on top and finish 3 minutes in the oven so the noodles curl up.
Rest 3 minutes and serve with allioli.

d: A meat and potato stew common in Pakistan and other South Asian cuisines; this version uses lamb.
s: Brown the sliced onions in the oil for 10 minutes. Add the chopped garlic and ginger, then the cubed meat.
Add the tomatoes, cumin, coriander, turmeric, chili and salt. Cook 8 minutes, stirring.
Add the water and simmer, covered, 60 to 75 minutes until the meat is almost tender.
Add the potatoes in chunks and continue 20 to 25 minutes, until tender.
Stir in the garam masala and adjust the liquid to the consistency you like. Serve with rice or flatbread.

d: Large dumplings of raw and cooked potato filled with salt pork and onion seasoned with allspice, poached and served with melted butter and lingonberries.
s: Sauté the pork and onion with the allspice; let cool.
Mix both potatoes, the flour and salt into a pliable dough.
Shape 12 balls, hollow them out, fill with the pork mixture and close.
Poach 15 to 20 minutes in simmering salted water until they float.
Serve with melted butter and lingonberry jam.

d: Pork leg braised for hours in a sweet soy sauce with star anise and cinnamon, served sliced over rice with a braised egg, pickled mustard greens and chili-vinegar sauce.
s: Blanch the pork 10 minutes and rinse.
Caramelize the palm sugar, then add the pounded garlic and cilantro roots.
Add the soy sauces, spices and water to cover, then the pork.
Simmer 2½ to 3 hours, adding the eggs for the last hour.
Slice and serve over rice with an egg, the pickled greens and a chili-garlic-vinegar sauce.

d: An Italian soup of small pasta and white beans; a vegetarian version not tied to any one region.
s: Sauté the finely diced onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 7 minutes.
Add the garlic, tomatoes and rosemary; cook 5 minutes, then pour in the broth and beans.
Simmer 10 minutes. Mash about a third of the beans in the pot to thicken.
Add the pasta and cook according to the package, stirring and adding broth if needed. Remove the rosemary, season and serve.

d: Chicken pieces marinated in yogurt, onion, lemon and saffron, grilled over coals and served with chelow rice and grilled tomatoes.
s: Mix the grated onion, yogurt, lemon juice, half the saffron and the salt.
Marinate the chicken at least 4 hours.
Thread the chicken and tomatoes onto skewers.
Grill 12 to 15 minutes, basting with the saffron butter.
Serve with white rice and sumac.
